## Write here, build with `make`

:::: {.columns-1-1}

::: {.column}
::: {.no-header}
| | |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `##`        | a new slide                |
| `#`         | a section divider slide    |
| `---`       | another slide, same title  |
| `. . .`     | reveal the rest on a click |
| `::: notes` | speaker notes; press **S** |
:::
:::

::: {.column}
::: {.no-header}
| | |
|:-------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `make`         | render `out/talk.html`       |
| `make preview` | reloads as you save          |
| `make check`   | catches content off the edge |
| `make png`     | one PNG per slide, to read   |
| `make all`     | HTML, PDF and PPTX           |
:::
:::

::::

::: {.highlight}
The look is one line of `_quarto.yml` — `theme: [default, themes/nord.scss]`.
All ten stylesheets travel inside this folder.
:::

::: notes
Nothing load-bearing goes in a notes block: reveal hides it in print, so it
reaches neither the PDF nor the PPTX. Press **S** for the presenter window —
notes, a timer, the next slide — and **X** to draw the slide boundary.
:::

## A figure is the slide, not an illustration

:::: {.columns-2-3}

::: {.column}
Keep this side to a claim, not a narration.

- A point worth making
- One that needs an [emphasis]{.alert}
- One that can stay [quieter]{.muted}

Give an image a width **or** a height. Never both — the aspect ratio is data.
:::

::: {.column}
::: {.fig}
[Planet sizes, drawn to one scale]{.caption}

![](attach/solar-system.jpg){width="680px"}

[Encyclopædia Britannica]{.credit}

[Distances are not to scale]{.below}
:::
:::

::::

::: {.highlight}
`.caption` names the panel above it; `.credit` sets the source at its edge.
:::

`.media-row` is a grid: label in one column, frames in the other. Set

## Three things, side by side

::::: {.columns-1-1-1}

:::: {.column}
::: {.card}
**Question**

What is not working, and for whom

[scope]{.pill}
:::
::::

:::: {.column}
::: {.card}
**Approach**

What we changed, and how we measured it

[method]{.pill}
:::
::::

:::: {.column}
::: {.card}
**Result**

What came out, and the number behind it

[+18%]{.pill}
:::
::::

:::::

::: {.highlight}
`.card` boxes a group; `.pill` tags it inline.

## Text, numbers, code and maths

:::: {.columns-1-1}

::: {.column}
#### Subheadings start at `####`

Body text with `inline code`, a [link](https://quarto.org) and **bold** where a
claim needs it. Maths is sized to the body, so $\bar{x} = n^{-1}\sum_i x_i$ sits
inside a sentence and a result gets its own line:

$$ \sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2 $$

> A sentence somebody else wrote, set as a blockquote.
:::

::: {.column}
| Method | Samples | Accuracy |
|:---------------|-------:|--------:|
| Baseline       |  1,000 |     71% |
| + new features |  1,000 |     84% |
| + more data    | 10,000 |     89% |

```python
def accuracy(correct, total):
    return correct / total
```

::: {.small}
`.small` for a block that has to give way, `.tiny` below that. The stylesheet
colours the code from its own palette, so the listing follows the theme.
:::
:::
